<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard binary package for `ocenaudio-bin`, sourcing a prebuilt tarball from the official `ocenaudio.com` domain via HTTPS. The `source` array contains a direct download URL with version substitution, which is resolved using the declared `pkgver`. There are no command substitutions, remote code executions, or network operations in the global scope or within a `pkgver()` function — in fact, `pkgver()` is absent and the version is hardcoded.

Checksums are provided via `sha512sums`, so integrity verification will occur during source fetching. Even if they were skipped (which they are not), that alone would not make this step unsafe, as extraction without execution is acceptable under `--nobuild --noprepare`. No code executes during sourcing beyond variable assignments, all of which use static, inline values. The `package()` function is irrelevant here due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so its contents are not evaluated in this phase.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and verify the source archive without executing any potentially malicious code.
</details>

data.reasoning: Two models (qwen3-235b and deepseek-v4-flash) successfully completed audits and both found the package safe. The PKGBUILD is a standard binary package that downloads a precompiled tarball from the official ocenaudio.com domain over HTTPS with SHA-512 checksum verification. No code execution occurs during source fetch, no suspicious commands or obfuscation in the package() function, and the binary payload is correctly skipped as unauditable. The three inconclusive reports are all tool errors (403, 429, parse error) and carry no verdict signal per the audit rules.
coverage_issues: thinkingmachines/inkling:free failed with 403 error (model not available for agentic harnesses)
z-ai/glm-5.2:free failed with 429 error (upstream rate limit)
openrouter/free failed with parse error (model output didn't match expected format)
learnings: Tool infrastructure errors (403, 429, parse failures) should be distinguished from audit findings and excluded from verdict calculation
For -bin packages, models correctly skip binary payloads and focus on PKGBUILD - this is appropriate behavior
Models should be prompted to strictly follow the expected XML output format to avoid parse errors
Rate-limited or unavailable models should trigger automatic retry or fallback rather than marking the entire audit inconclusive
